assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson is among the clearest discoveries in modern physics: nature answered a sharp question posed by theory decades earlier, completing the Standard Model. It puts the discovery first, which is how I want to judge a prize. The 2013 prize recognised the theory but not the experimental finding, which leaves a clear gap.
assessment.attribution: Decisive credit belongs to two huge collaborations. The three listed names are the founding or early leaders of ATLAS and CMS and can represent both experiments in a fair configuration, but the people who conceived the detectors and the analyses are far more numerous. I would want expert reports on who shaped each detector concept.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature. Independent confirmation by two experiments, with properties measured over more than a decade and consistent with the Standard Model. Timely, and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether leadership roles are an acceptable proxy for decisive contribution in a collaboration of thousands.
Whether a prize for the observation, after the 2013 theory prize, is seen as completing the story or as redundant.
I rely on memory for the roles of the three listed individuals and have not verified them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Direct imaging of the shadow of a supermassive black hole connects strong-field gravity to observation in a way that anyone can see, and it has an existential dimension for how we picture the universe. The result is original in its instrumental achievement (global VLBI at 1.3 mm) and gives a direct test of the near-horizon region, a topic close to my own research.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the Event Horizon Telescope effort and Zensus built the European VLBI infrastructure. This is a plausible three-person set, but the EHT collaboration is very large and the roles of technical and theory contributors are open to dispute.
assessment.maturity: M87* (2019) and Sgr A* (2022) both imaged, with polarisation follow-ups. Interpretation is stable at the level of a ring consistent with general relativity, but tests of alternatives remain limited by resolution, so the confirmation is strong yet not yet precision.
uncertainties: How tightly the images constrain deviations from general relativity or horizonless alternatives.
Fair allocation of credit between concept, instrument leadership and the large collaboration.
Whether the committee judges the finding to be mature enough, only a few years after the Sgr A* result.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane as sources, opened a new window on the universe. It is a discovery driven by nature, made with an instrument of unusual originality (a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice).
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove IceCube, and Spiering is a long-time leader in neutrino astronomy and the earlier Baikal and AMANDA efforts. A two-person prize is possible, but other contributors to the early detector concepts, such as those behind DUMAND and AMANDA, could complicate it.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed over a decade, with the diffuse flux, a source association and a Galactic-plane signal. Source populations remain only partly understood, so the field is still young, but the central discovery is solid.
uncertainties: Whether the source identification evidence is judged as firm as the diffuse-flux detection.
Credit for the early pioneering experiments and the wider collaboration.
I have not verified the exact attribution of the first concept papers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators, and its observation in HgTe, gave a new class of matter and a rare case of theory and experiment meeting cleanly. It is original and has had a huge influence on condensed matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction, and Molenkamp's group did the decisive observation, which supports a balanced theory plus experiment trio. Other credited work on HgTe (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) is not in the supplied names, which makes the allocation incomplete, and I can only choose from the listed names.
assessment.maturity: Mature after nearly two decades, with multiple independent materials confirmations. The 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions, so there is a real question of how this is distinguished from it.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 topological prize and the exclusion of other theorists from the supplied credits.
Practical impact is still limited, which matters less to me than the clarity of the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, with the magic-wavelength idea, reached a stability and accuracy beyond the caesium standard and enable tests of fundamental constants and relativity at the millimetre scale. Strong precision-measurement value and a clean, original concept.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice, and Ye's group took it to the highest performance. This is a coherent two-person configuration, with possible overlap with ion-clock work already recognised in 2012.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely reproduced at many laboratories, with the SI second redefinition in preparation. Timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier prize for methods to measure and manipulate single quantum systems.
Whether Ye's other contributions blur the attribution of the lattice-clock concept.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP turned the CMB into a precision laboratory for the cosmological model, fixing the age, geometry and composition of the universe. This is the observational foundation for the dark energy and dark matter questions I work with.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page designed key instrument elements and Spergel led the interpretation. The configuration is reasonable, but Planck confirmed and refined the results, and the 2006 and 2019 prizes have already covered CMB anisotropy and cosmology, so the added novelty is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and confirmed independently by Planck and ground experiments. The question is whether this is too late or already covered.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 COBE prize and the 2019 cosmology prize.
Whether leadership and instrument roles are decisive relative to other WMAP team members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened an entire field of moire materials. Theory and experiment are tightly linked.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery. This is a natural configuration, though Cao and others who did the experiment are not listed, and I can use only the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Quickly and broadly reproduced, but the microscopic mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated and the field is under ten years old, so it is probably early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism remains unsettled.
Whether the prize is premature relative to other candidates with longer track records.
Credit for graduate student and early collaborators.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The double pulsar gives several independent strong-field tests of general relativity in a single system, extending the Hulse-Taylor result with a sharper and richer laboratory. Nature supplied the clue, and the result fits my view that gravity needs observational anchors.
assessment.attribution: Burgay found the system, Lyne led the Jodrell Bank group, and Kramer led the timing and the tests. This is a plausible three-person split, but the relation to the 1993 prize may make the committee see it as an extension rather than a new discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with more than fifteen years of timing and consistent agreement with general relativity at the 0.01 percent level.
uncertainties: Novelty relative to the 1993 Hulse and Taylor prize.
The relative weight of discovery versus the later timing experiments.
